record.original_question: Study constructions and objects in constructive mathematics from the viewpoint of program-size complexity, where constructive mathematics is taken to mean mathematics together with the principle that existence coincides with computability.

evidence.quote: 16. Constructive mathematics is essentially mathematics plus the assumption that "existence = computability". Constructions and objects in constructive mathematics have been studied from the point of view of dynamic complexities and it would be interesting to study them also from the point of view of program-size complexity. (C. Calude)

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let constructive mathematics be understood as ordinary mathematics together with the foundational principle that existence coincides with computability, i.e. an object is said to exist only if it can be produced by an algorithm. For a partial computable function (interpreter) U on finite binary strings, define the program-size (Kolmogorov) complexity of a finite object x by K_U(x) = min{ |p| : U(p) = x }, taking U to be an optimal universal machine so that K = K_U is well-defined up to an additive constant. More generally, for an infinite object (such as a real number, a sequence, or a constructively defined set) presented by a computable approximation, define its program-size complexity profile via the complexities K(x_n) of its finite approximations x_n.

Develop a systematic theory of constructive mathematics from the viewpoint of program-size complexity: for the standard constructions and objects of constructive mathematics (constructive real numbers, constructive functions on [0,1], constructive metric spaces, constructive measure theory, constructive algebraic structures, witnesses of constructive existence proofs, and constructive proofs of classical theorems), determine the program-size complexity of natural representatives, establish sharp upper and lower bounds, and identify intrinsic complexity invariants of these constructions. In particular, classify which constructive objects admit representatives of low program-size complexity and which necessarily require high complexity, and compare these complexity-theoretic invariants with the previously studied dynamic (time/space) complexity invariants of the same objects.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a broad research program proposed as an open problem in algorithmic information theory by C. Calude. While individual program-size complexity results for specific constructive objects (e.g. computable reals, Chaitin's Omega) have been obtained, no comprehensive program-size complexity theory of constructive mathematics as a whole has been established, and the problem appears to remain open as a research direction.
